## ⚠️ The two-lane in-flight intersection the triage ruling demands — run, and **PARTIAL**

This card takes the **cross-domain exception path**, so the claiming seat owes an in-flight intersection against **both** `domain:engine` and `domain:cli`, ⛔ not just its own lane.

- **`domain:engine`** in flight: #18318 (`packages/formula/src/`, PR #18736 in the merge queue) · #18715 (`scripts/`). ⇒ **Disjoint** from this surface.
- **`domain:cli`** in flight: **#18650**, **#18590**, **#18540** — all `pm:dispatched`, all assigned to `os-support-ai`.

⛔⛔ **None of those three carries a `Claim:` comment**, so their declared file surfaces ⛔ **cannot be read**, and the intersection the ruling asks for cannot be completed as specified. ⚠️ That is a half-state on the `domain:cli` lane; it is ⛔ **not this seat's to repair** and it is recorded here so it is not mistaken for a clean reading.

⭐ **What was done instead, and its limit:** the one card whose subject could plausibly reach `packages/rest` — **#18540**, 「a NON-sandboxed crash at `/api/v1/actions`」 — was read by content. It names `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts` and mentions neither `rest-api-plugin.ts` nor `resolve-authz-context.ts` (**0** hits). ⇒ Ruled out on content. The other two (#18650, an identity-auth checklist; #18590, nightly rerun safety) are ⛔ **not proven** disjoint — only implausible.

⇒ ⚠️ **If you find someone else's edit in either of your two files, STOP and report it.** ⛔ Do not assume this intersection cleared you; it half did, and you have been told which half.

## ⛔ Take the 5 lines from the census, ⛔ not from this card and ⛔ not from a fresh sweep

The card is explicit: the exact 5 sentences come from **#17379's census, comment `5704455410`** (22332 characters, sentence by sentence). ⛔ Do not re-run your own sweep, and ⛔ do not take line numbers from the card body — the card says its own anchors are readings, ⛔ not identifiers.

⛔ **Out of scope, and triage ruled it so**: the 107 「true but for a stale reason」 lines and the 23 「still true」 lines. The census already proved they are ⛔ not defects.

## ⚠️⚠️ Three of the sites are MACHINE ASSERTIONS, ⛔ not prose

Inherited verbatim from #17379 and repeated because a prose-only edit turns them red:

- `serve-capability-vocabulary.test.ts:92` and `doctor-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts:197` assert `edition === 'enterprise'`;
- `harness.host-resolution.test.ts:288,319` pin operator strings with a regex.

⭐⭐ **And one of them carries a prior decision you must read before touching it:** `doctor-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts:188-194` argues at length that the line is **deliberate** — 「deliberately not relaxed to match the prose reword」. ⇒ ⛔ **Editing it without reading that passage is overturning a judgement someone already made.** If your reading says it should move anyway, say so with the argument, ⛔ do not just move it.

## The deliverable is ONE adjective, chosen once

Triage kept this as a single card for a stated reason, quoted from the execution seat that raised it:

> 它是一次**原子的形容词裁定**;分成两张,两个席位可以合法地选出不同的形容词,树上就多一处新的不一致。

⇒ Pick the adjective **once**, apply it to all five, and say in the report what you picked and why the alternatives lose. ⛔ Five locally-reasonable choices is the failure mode this card exists to prevent.

## Grading

`Clause-②: no` and `skip-changeset` expected — the sites are prose and test assertions about a private subclass, with no accept set and no published surface moving. ⚠️ Both are the seat's reading, ⛔ not findings: measure each the way your role file prescribes, with a positive control, and regrade at column 0 of the PR body if your own diff contradicts it. ⚠️ `packages/core` and `packages/rest` both publish, so ⛔ do not assume `skip-changeset` — a changed **runtime string** could ship.

`needs:contract-review` is the seat's label: ⛔ do not hang it, unhang it, or wait on it.

## ⚠️ Two rules from the CURRENT charter your loaded role file does not carry

`check-harness-current.mjs` exits **1** in this container — `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` is not at `origin/main` here. ⛔ These are the role file's own current text, ⛔ not the seat overriding it:

1. **Copy the claim's `Clause-②:` line to column 0 of the PR body in the opening write** — `Check Changeset` reads the body, ⛔ not the card.
2. **Write the PR body exactly once, in the `POST /pulls` stroke; ⛔ never `PATCH` it.**

Everything else in the role file governs as loaded; where it and this dispatch differ, **the role file wins** and you say so in the report.

## ⭐ The adjective, and the move the card did not ask for

One adjective, chosen once, applied to all five: **`licence-gated`**.

It is the tree's own spelling — **13** files carry it on `origin/main`, against **0** for the American `license-gated` (a control that fires in both directions on one instrument) — and, more importantly, it is the property that **discriminates** under ADR-0132 D3: the open-core build in this repo is not gated; the subclass cloud resolves the same name to is.

⭐⭐ **And then it did something finer than the card asked.** At the three `packages/rest` sites the adjective sat on the bare package **name**, so it added the referent noun `subclass` with it:

> otherwise the repair trades one false reading (「this package is private」) for another (「this package needs a licence」)

⇒ The two `packages/core` sites already named the mounted instance and take the adjective alone. **That distinction is the whole value of doing this as one ruling** — a seat applying one word uniformly to five sites would have introduced the second false reading at exactly three of them.

## The alternatives were argued down, ⛔ not skipped

- **`enterprise`** ⛔ does not discriminate at all — `tenancy-posture.ts` uses 「the enterprise `@objectstack/organizations` runtime」 for the package required to **activate** a multi-org posture, which since ADR-0132 is the **open** one. It would have added five lines to the 107-line stale-reason population the census already ruled out of scope.
- **Keeping `cloud-private`** (the census's option C) states the **package** is private — the exact claim ADR-0132 falsified and a six-PR campaign removed everywhere else.
- **Dropping the adjective** is right for an operator-facing message and is *already ruled so* — but that ruling is about a message whose **reader is unknown**, while these five are measurement narratives whose subject is named. ⭐ And two of them contrast 「objectstack#15163 measured it on the framework」 with 「cloud#1982 reproduced it with the real X」 — **with no adjective that contrast collapses into the same artifact twice.**
- **`entitled`** already has a different job (「Open code, entitled activation」).

The dispatch flagged `doctor-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts:188-194`, which argues at length that its line is **deliberately** not relaxed, and said editing it without reading that passage would overturn a decision someone already made.

⇒ The dev read it, and concluded its argument **is the same reading this diff applies** ⇒ ⛔ no argument to move it, and it is untouched. ⭐ That is better than either of the failure modes: it neither edited it blindly nor avoided it out of caution.

**Verified independently**: all three machine-assertion files live in `packages/cli/` and `packages/verify/` — outside the declared surface, so none could be in this diff by construction:
`packages/cli/test/serve-capability-vocabulary.test.ts` · `packages/cli/src/commands/doctor-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts` · `packages/verify/src/harness.host-resolution.test.ts`.

The dev noted that `docs/adr/0132-*.md:3` still reads **`Status: Proposed`** while this diff 「leans on ADR-0132 as settled law」. ⭐ It raised that against its own change rather than letting it pass. The ADR's own header is blunt about the stakes:

> **Status**: Proposed … awaiting the maintainer's hand-merge, **which is itself the acceptance act** for a governed surface (Prime Directive #14). ⛔ Nothing below is settled until this record merges.

⇒ **The record HAS merged**, and by that sentence's own terms the merge is the acceptance. Measured: `docs/adr/0132-…md` is on `origin/main` at commit `c677cda816`, authored by **Jack Zhuang** — a human hand-merge of a governed surface, which is exactly the act the ADR names.

⇒ ⭐ **`Status: Proposed` is a stale label, ⛔ not an unsettled record**, and this diff's premise stands. The stale line already has a carrier on #17379's report; ⛔ this seat does not refile it.

## ⭐ The changeset control is the good kind

⛔ Not 「grep found nothing」. The dev proved the **channel exists** before reporting a zero on it: comment prose **does** reach published output — `cloud#1982` sits at `packages/rest/dist/index.d.ts:421`, out of a JSDoc on an exported declaration — and the exported symbols hit in `dist` as expected. Then `licence-gated` in `packages/core/dist` + `packages/rest/dist` → **exit 1, zero hits**.

⇒ The channel exists, the control fires, none of the five edited comments is on it. `skip-changeset` and `Clause-②: no` both hold as measurements.

⏹️ **No ablation, and none was owed** — comment prose with no guard, no assertion and no runtime behaviour to mutate. ⭐ Saying so beats a decorative mutation.

## Findings

⏹️ Three `noted, not filed`, all correctly classed and each with an honest successor — including 「**NONE queued** — the census's class-3 lane table lists no `packages/rest` lane」, which is a better answer than an invented carrier. The third (ADR-0132's stale status) is explicitly *not refiled* because #17379's report already carries it.

`mcp_calls` **0** · REST writes **3**. Label written: `skip-changeset` only, additive, read back. ⛔ `needs:contract-review` untouched — correct at `Clause-②: no`. Lint was the **full repo scan**, so ⛔ no narrowing evidence is owed.

⇒ ⏹️ Ready + queue **once CI converges** (16 still running). This seat follows it to **MERGED**.
